newsitem.title: JAPAN: Stocks, rates reflect Japan recovery -- BOJ quoted.
newsitem.headline: Stocks, rates reflect Japan recovery -- BOJ quoted.

text.p: A rise in Japan's stock market and long-term interest rates is in line with the recovery in the economy, Masayuki Matsushima, director of the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) research and statistics department, was quoted as saying by Monday's Nihon Keizai Shimbun.

Asked about the Nikkei average's climb to above 20,000 and a recent rise in long-term interest rates to above 2.50 percent, the paper quoted Matsushima as saying that caution about the economy had been corrected and was in line with the recovery.
Concern about Japan's financial system was disappearing and as a result, markets were now able to appraise frankly the uptrend in the economy, Matsushima said.
He also said that private demand was becoming firmer, exports were rising and that the mechanism for cyclical recovery in demand, production and income was becoming clearer.

The effects of a rise in the sales tax on April 1 would make growth slow temporarily and it was important to watch to see when the fall-off in consumer spending would slow, he said. The improvement in the employment situation and wages was a gradual one but was unlikely to be threatened, he said.

However he added that consumption was affected to a large extent by sentiment and the effect of an end to special income tax cuts and an expected drop in disposable income after rises in medical insurance costs were also problems.
